translationRepairs: The chief offices, in descending rank, were qu'lüchuo, abo, jielifa, tutun, and hojin—each held hereditarily by a lineage without a fixed number of incumbents, passing from elder to younger when the officeholder died.

The chief offices, in descending rank, were qu'lüchuo, abo, jielifa, tutun, and qijin (irkin)—each held hereditarily without a fixed number of incumbents; when a father or elder brother died, his sons or younger brothers inherited.
俟斤 is qijin (Turkic irkin), not "hojin"; 父兄死則子弟承襲 means sons or younger brothers inherited when a father or elder brother died, not "from elder to younger".
That same month Shibi died. His son Shibieli was judged too young to rule and was made nibushi shad, assigned to the eastern wing of the confederation directly north of Youzhou.
That same month Shibi died. His son Shibobi was judged too young to rule and was made Nibu shad, assigned to the eastern wing of the confederation directly north of Youzhou.
什缽苾 reads Shibobi, not "Shibieli"; 泥步設 is the title Nibu shad ("nibushi shad" duplicates 設). (The literal field has the same errors.)
His younger brother Heli'er shad was raised to the throne as Chuluo Khan.
His younger brother, the Qilifu shad, was raised to the throne as Chuluo Khan.
俟利弗設 reads Qilifu shad; "Heli'er" is not a reading of 俟利弗. (The literal field has the same error.)
Earlier, Empress Xiao of the late Sui emperor Yang and Yang Zhengdao, son of the executed Prince of Qi Yang Jian, had been held captive by the rebel Dou Jiande.
Earlier, Empress Xiao of the late Sui emperor Yang and Yang Zhengdao, son of Yang Jian, Prince of Qi, had been held captive by the rebel Dou Jiande.
The Chinese 齊王暕之子政道 does not say the Prince of Qi was executed; "executed" is an addition. Also clarifies that Yang Jian is the Prince of Qi.
Soon afterward Chuluo died. Princess Yicheng, finding her son Aoshe shad unfit to rule, passed him over and enthroned Chuluo's younger brother Tujie as Jieli Khan.
Soon afterward Chuluo died. Because his son Aoshe shad was ugly and weak, Princess Yicheng set him aside and enthroned Chuluo's younger brother Duobi as Jieli Khan.
咄苾 reads Duobi, not "Tujie"; 醜弱 means ugly and weak, not merely "unfit to rule"; 其子 most naturally refers to the just-mentioned Chuluo, not to the princess.
In Wude year 3, Jieli again married Princess Yicheng, installed Shibi's son Shibieli as Tuli Khan, and sent envoys to announce Chuluo's death.
In Wude year 3, Jieli again married Princess Yicheng, installed Shibi's son Shibobi as Tuli Khan, and sent envoys to announce Chuluo's death.
什缽苾 reads Shibobi, not "Shibieli". (The literal field has the same error.)
Jieli's envoys spoke with insolent arrogance, and his demands knew no limit.
Jieli's words were insolent and arrogant, and his demands knew no limit.
頡利言辭悖傲 says Jieli’s own words were insolent; the Chinese does not mention envoys.
Earlier, Duke of Hanyang Su Gui, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshan, and Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Sun Shunde had been sent as envoys to the Turks, and Jieli had detained them all.
Earlier, Duke of Hanyang Su Gui, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu, and Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Zhangsun Shunde had been sent as envoys to the Turks, and Jieli had detained them all.
鄭元璹 is Zheng Yuanshu (璹 shú), and 長孫順德 has the double surname Zhangsun, not "Sun". (The literal field has the same errors.)
Checked by Li Da'en's victory, Jieli took fright, released Sun Shunde, and again sued for peace.
Checked by Li Da'en's victory, Jieli took fright, released Zhangsun Shunde, and again sued for peace.
順德 here is 長孫順德 (Zhangsun Shunde, double surname Zhangsun), not "Sun Shunde".

On the jimao day he pushed on to Gaoling. Campaign commander and Left Martial Guard General Yuchi Jingde met him at Jingyang and routed his army, capturing the hojin Ashide Wumochuo and taking more than a thousand heads.

On the jimao day he pushed on to Gaoling. Campaign commander and Left Martial Guard General Yuchi Jingde met him at Jingyang and routed his army, capturing the qijin (irkin) Ashide Wumochuo and taking more than a thousand heads.
俟斤 is qijin (Turkic irkin), not "hojin". (The literal field has the same error.)
The prince told him: "I sealed peace with the Turks in person, and you broke it. I have nothing to be ashamed of.
Taizong told him: "I sealed peace with the Turks in person, and you broke it. I have nothing to be ashamed of.
By this point (Wude 9, after the accession; cf. 朕又新登九五 in s0103) 太宗 had already ascended the throne, so "the prince" is the wrong title.
Sili, terrified, begged for his life, but the prince refused and had him imprisoned in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
Sili, terrified, begged for his life, but Taizong refused and had him imprisoned in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
By this point 太宗 had already ascended the throne (cf. s0103 朕又新登九五), so "the prince" is the wrong title.

Riding with Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Shilian, Grand Counselor Fang Xuanling, and General Zhou Fan on six horses, the prince came to the Wei River, spoke with Jieli across the water, and rebuked him for breaking faith.

Riding with Director of the Chancellery Gao Shilian, Director of the Secretariat Fang Xuanling, and General Zhou Fan on six horses, the emperor came to the Wei River, spoke with Jieli across the water, and rebuked him for breaking faith.

侍中 is Director of the Chancellery (not Attendant-in-Ordinary) and 中書令 is Director of the Secretariat (not Grand Counselor); Taizong had already ascended the throne (cf. s0103), so "the prince" is the wrong title.
Soon the main armies came up behind the prince. Jieli saw their strength and learned that Sili was a prisoner—and fear seized him.
Soon the main armies arrived one after another. Jieli saw their strength and learned that Sili was a prisoner—and fear seized him.
眾軍繼至 says only that the armies arrived in succession; "behind the prince" adds a wrong title, since Taizong was already emperor.
Jieli for the first time styled himself a subject. He had married an imperial princess and asked to perform the rites due a son-in-law.
Jieli for the first time styled himself a subject and asked to marry an imperial princess and perform the rites due a son-in-law.
尚公主，請修婿禮 is a request to wed a princess and perform son-in-law rites; the English wrongly says he had already married one.
Because Jieli had sued for peace and then again aided Liang Shidu, an edict ordered Minister of War Li Jing and Protector-General of Daizhou Zhang Gongjin to advance by the Dingxiang route.
Because Jieli had sued for peace and then again aided Liang Shidu, an edict ordered Minister of War Li Jing and Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou Zhang Gongjin to advance by the Dingxiang route.
都督 is an area commander-in-chief, not a Protector-General (都護). (The literal field has the same error.)

Protector-General of Bingzhou Li Shiji and Right Martial Guard General Qiu Xinggong were to advance by the Tonghan route; Left Martial Guard Grand General Chai Shao by the Jinhe route; Wei Xiaojie by the Heng'an route; and Xue Wanche by the Changwu route—all under Li Jing's command.

都督 is an area commander-in-chief, not a Protector-General (都護); the Chinese name is 李勣 (Li Ji), not Li Shiji.
In the twelfth month Tuli Khan, Yushe she, Yinnaitele, and others led their followers to surrender.
In the twelfth month Tuli Khan, the Yushe shad, the Yinnai tegin, and others led their followers to surrender.
廕奈特勒 is the Yinnai tegin (特勒 = tegin), not a single name "Yinnaitele"; 設 is rendered shad elsewhere in this chapter.
Tuli Khan Shebishi was the legitimate son of Shibi Khan and Jieli's nephew.
Tuli Khan Shibobi was the legitimate son of Shibi Khan and Jieli's nephew.
什缽苾 reads Shibobi, not "Shebishi". (The literal field has the same error; the Chinese 可法 is a graphic error for 可汗.)
I am changing the old way so that China may know lasting peace and your clan may endure. That is why I appoint you Protector-General.
I am changing the old way so that China may know lasting peace and your clan may endure. That is why I appoint you area commander-in-chief.
都督 is an area commander-in-chief (dudu), not a Protector-General (都護). (The literal field has the same error.)

賀邏鶻 is a single three-syllable name, Heluohu (鶻 hú); "Heluo Huhu" duplicates the last syllable. (The literal field has the same error.)

They were therefore moved to Hebei, and Right Bulwark General, Area Commander of Huazhou, and Prince of Huaihua Simo was installed as Yimi Nishou Kelibo Khan, given the surname Li, and ordered to lead his followers and establish his headquarters in Hebei.

Many memorials also argued that settling Turks within China was a bad idea. They were therefore moved to Hebei, and Right Bulwark General, Area Commander of Huazhou, and Prince of Huaihua Simo was installed as Yimi Nishu Qilibi Khan, given the surname Li, and ordered to lead his followers and establish his headquarters in Hebei.
泥孰 reads Nishu (孰 shú), not "Nishou"; 侯利苾 is evidently a graphic error for 俟利苾 Qilibi (cf. Qilifu), and "Kelibo" is not a reading of either. (The literal field has the same errors.)
Emperor Taizong sent Minister of Food Granaries Guo Siyuan to deliver to Xueyantuo an imperial letter bearing the seal, which read:
Emperor Taizong sent Minister of Food Granaries Guo Siben to deliver to Xueyantuo an imperial letter bearing the seal, which read:
郭嗣本 is Guo Siben (本 běn), not "Guo Siyuan". (The literal field has the same error.)
He also appointed Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Zhong as Left Wise Prince and Left Martial Guard General Ashina Nishou as Right Wise Prince.
He also appointed Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Zhong as Left Wise Prince and Left Martial Guard General Ashina Nishu as Right Wise Prince.
阿史那泥孰 reads Ashina Nishu (孰 shú), not "Nishou".

When the Son of Heaven broke the Turks he should have taken them as slaves for the people. Instead he nourishes them like sons—and Jieshe'er rebelled anyway. These people have beasts' hearts and cannot be trusted.

When the Son of Heaven broke the Turks he should have taken them as slaves for the people. Instead he nourishes them like sons—and Jiesheshuai rebelled anyway. These people have beasts' hearts and cannot be trusted.
結社率 is Jiesheshuai, not "Jieshe'er". (The literal field has the same error.)

In the twenty-third year of Zhenguan he sent Colonel of the Right Valiant Guard Gao Kan secretly to lead Huihe, Pugu, and other forces in a surprise attack. Chiefs Geluolu Nishou Quesili fa, Baisai fu Chumukun Moheduo sijin, and others turned against Chebi with their tribes and surrendered one after another.

In the twenty-third year of Zhenguan he sent Commandant of the Right Valiant Guard Gao Kan secretly to lead Huihe, Pugu, and other forces in a surprise attack. Chiefs such as the Geluolu Nishu Que Qilifa and Basaifu, the Chumukun Moheduo Qijin, turned against Chebi with their tribes and surrendered one after another.
泥孰 is Nishu; 闕俟利發 is Que Qilifa (俟利發 = qilifa/eltäbär), not "Quesili fa"; 拔塞匐 is Basaifu, not "Baisai fu"; 俟斤 is qijin, not "sijin". (The literal field has the same errors.)

In the first year of Tiaolu, within the Chanyu Protectorate the Turk chiefs Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi of two tribes rose in rebellion together, installed Nishou fu as khan, and twenty-four prefectures joined them.

In the first year of Tiaolu, within the Chanyu Protectorate the Turk chiefs Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi of two tribes rose in rebellion together, installed Nishufu as khan, and twenty-four prefectures joined them.
泥孰匐 is the single name Nishufu, not "Nishou fu". (The literal field has the same error.)
Nishou fu was killed by his own followers, and Fengzhi was captured as well before the army returned.
Nishufu was killed by his own followers, and Fengzhi was captured as well before the army returned.
泥孰匐 is Nishufu, not "Nishou fu". (The literal field has the same error.)
Emperor Gaozong sent Chamberlain for Dependencies Xiao Siye and Colonel of the Right Palace Guard Li Jingjia against them, but Wenfu defeated them and more than ten thousand soldiers were killed.
Emperor Gaozong sent Chamberlain for Dependencies Xiao Siye and General of the Right Qianniu Guard Li Jingjia against them, but Wenfu defeated them and more than ten thousand soldiers were killed.
右千牛將軍 is a general of the Right Qianniu Guard, not a "Colonel". (The literal field has the same error.)
The court again ordered Pei Xingjian, with Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, and Li Wenliang, to suppress them.
The court again ordered Pei Xingjian, with Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, and Li Wenjian, to suppress them.
李文暕 is Li Wenjian (暕 jiǎn), not "Li Wenliang". (The literal field has the same error.)
Xingjian then marched Fuzhen as a prisoner to the capital and had him beheaded at the Eastern Market.
Xingjian then marched Funian as a prisoner to the capital and had him beheaded at the Eastern Market.
伏念 is Funian, as in the preceding sentences, not "Fuzhen". (The literal field has the same error.)
In 683, Ashina Gutulu of the Türks rose in rebellion once more.
In the second year of Yongchun (683), Ashina Gudulu of the Turks rose in rebellion once more.
骨咄祿 is rendered Gudulu throughout this passage, not "Gutulu"; the reign date 永淳二年 is restored. (The literal field has "Gutulu" too.)
Empress Wu was furious and renamed Gudulu Bucelü ('Never-Die Lu').
Empress Wu was furious and changed Gudulu's name to Buzulu (不卒祿, 'Lu who comes to no good end').
不卒祿 reads Buzulu; "Bucelü" is not a reading of the characters, and "Never-Die" inverts the insult (不卒 = not to end well). (The literal field has the same romanization error.)

Soon they advanced against Ji, Tan, and other prefectures. Empress Wu appointed Director of the Household Wu Chonggui grand general of the Tianbing central route, Right Wuwei Guard General Shachuo Zhongyi forward grand general of the western route, and Youzhou Area Commander Zhang Renyuan grand general of the eastern route, with three hundred thousand men to strike them.

Soon they advanced against Gui, Tan, and other prefectures. Empress Wu appointed Director of the Household Wu Chonggui grand general of the Tianbing central route, Right Wuwei Guard General Shazha Zhongyi forward commander of the Tianbing western route, and Youzhou Area Commander Zhang Rendan commander of the Tianbing eastern route, with three hundred thousand men to strike them.
沙咤 is Shazha (咤 zhà), not "Shachuo"; 張仁亶 is Zhang Rendan as written (he was later renamed Renyuan); 媯 is Gui, not "Ji". (The literal field has the same errors.)
Shachuo Zhongyi, Rear Grand General Li Duozuo, and others all held large forces and confronted the rebels but did not dare to engage.
Shazha Zhongyi, Rear Commander Li Duozuo, and others all held large forces and confronted the rebels but did not dare to engage.
沙咤 is Shazha, not "Shachuo". (The literal field has the same error.)
In the second year Mochuo appointed his younger brother Dusibo left irkhan and Gudulu's son Moju right irkhan, each commanding more than twenty thousand horsemen.
In the second year Mochuo appointed his younger brother Dusifu Left Wing Shad and Gudulu's son Moju Right Wing Shad, each commanding more than twenty thousand horsemen.
察 here transcribes šad (= 設), not "irkhan"; 咄悉匐 is rendered Dusifu, as in the preceding chunk. (The literal field has the same issue.)
He also made his son Fuju lesser khan, ranking above both irkhans, with more than forty thousand horsemen of the Chumukun and other ten tribes under his command.
He also made his son Fuju lesser khan, ranking above both shads, with more than forty thousand horsemen of the Chumukun and other Ten Surnames under his command.
兩察 are the two shads just appointed, not "irkhans". (The literal field has the same issue.)
He also took the title Tuoxi Khan and from then on raided the frontier every year.
Fuju was also styled Tuoxi Khan, and from then on Mochuo raided the frontier every year.
The title 拓西可汗 continues the description of Fuju in the preceding sentence; the yearly raids are Mochuo’s. The draft makes the subject ambiguous.

The court appointed Right Suizheng Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong grand general of the Lingwu campaign route to guard against him and named Northern Anbei Area Commander Prince of Xiang Dan marshal of the Tianbing route to command the punitive armies. Before the armies marched, the raiders withdrew.

The court appointed Right Suzheng Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong grand general of the Lingwu campaign route to guard against him and named Dan, Prince of Xiang and Grand Area Commander-in-chief of Anbei, marshal of the Tianbing route to command the punitive armies. Before the armies marched, the raiders withdrew.
安北大都督 is Grand Area Commander-in-chief of Anbei; "Northern" is spurious; 相王旦 is Dan, Prince of Xiang; 肅政 is Suzheng. (The literal field has the same issues.)
In the third year of Chang'an Mochuo sent the envoy Mohedagan to ask that his daughter marry the crown prince's son.
In the third year of Chang'an Mochuo sent the envoy Mohe Dagan to ask that his daughter marry the crown prince's son.
莫賀達干 is the title-name Mohe Dagan (baga tarkan), parallel to Apo Dagan earlier in the chapter.
Mochuo sent the great chief Yilibeguhan to court with a thousand horses and tribute goods to thank the court for agreeing to the marriage.
Mochuo sent the great chief Yili Tanhan to court with a thousand horses and tribute goods to thank the court for agreeing to the marriage.
移力貪汗 reads Yili Tanhan; "Yilibeguhan" is not a reading of these characters. (The literal field has the same error.)
Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army Shacha Zhongyi fought a long defense, but the imperial force was beaten and more than six thousand soldiers died.
Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army Shazha Zhongyi fought a long defense, but the imperial force was beaten and more than six thousand soldiers died.
沙咤 is Shazha (咤 zhà), not "Shacha". (The literal field has the same error.)
Frontier generals such as Shachuo Zhongyi are fierce fighters but lack long-range vision. They are cavalry commanders by temperament and should not be entrusted with supreme command.
Frontier generals such as Shazha Zhongyi are fierce fighters but lack long-range vision. They are cavalry commanders by temperament and should not be entrusted with supreme command.
沙咤 is Shazha, not "Shachuo". (The literal field has the same error.)
I have heard that when Han appointed Zhe Du, the Xiongnu kept clear of the frontier;
I have heard that when Han appointed Zhi Du, the Xiongnu kept clear of the frontier;
郅都 is Zhi Du (郅 zhì), not "Zhe Du". (The literal field has the same error.)

Siyan refused to submit to the enemy and was posthumously honored as Chamberlain for Dependencies. The court then appointed Left Tunwei Guard Grand General Zhang Renyuan acting Right Censorate Chief Censor and grand general of the Shuofang route to defend against Mochuo.

Siyan refused to submit to the enemy and was posthumously honored as Chamberlain for Dependencies. The court then appointed Left Tunwei Guard Grand General Zhang Rendan acting Right Censorate Chief Censor and grand general of the Shuofang route to defend against Mochuo.
張仁亶 is Zhang Rendan as written (his later name Renyuan was adopted to avoid Ruizong’s taboo). (The literal field has the same substitution.)
Renyuan built the three Surrender-Accepting Cities beyond the river, blocking the southern route of Turk raids.
Rendan built the three Surrender-Accepting Cities beyond the river, blocking the southern route of Turk raids.
仁亶 is Rendan as written, not "Renyuan". (The literal field has the same substitution.)
Mochuo then sent his son Yang Wozhi tele to court and had him appointed Right Xiao Guard Extra Grand General.
Mochuo then sent his son Yang Wozhi Tegin to court and had him appointed Right Xiao Guard Extra Grand General.
特勒 is the Turkic title tegin, rendered "tegin" throughout this chapter, not "tele". (The literal field has the same rendering.)
In the second year of Kaiyuan (714), he sent his son Yi nie khan, Tong'e tele, and his son-in-law Huoba yilifa of the Shashi Ashibi clan with elite cavalry to besiege Beiting.
In the second year of Kaiyuan (714), he sent his son the Yinie Khan, Tong'e Tegin, and his younger sister's husband, the Huoba Jielifa Shi Ashibi, with elite cavalry to besiege Beiting.

妹婿 is a younger sister’s husband, not a son-in-law; 移涅可汗 is the Yinie Khan; 特勒 is tegin; 火拔頡利發石阿失畢 is the Huoba jielifa (eltäbär) named Shi Ashibi, not "Huoba yilifa of the Shashi Ashibi clan". (The literal field has the same errors.)
Right Xiao Guard General Guo Qianjin held the city in a stout defense, then sallied forth and captured Tong'e tele beneath the walls and beheaded him.
Right Xiao Guard General Guo Qianguan held the city in a stout defense, then sallied forth and captured Tong'e Tegin beneath the walls and beheaded him.
郭虔瓘 is Guo Qianguan (瓘 guàn), not "Guo Qianjin"; 特勒 is tegin. (The literal field has the same errors.)

Kutluk's son Kultegin rallied the old tribes, slaughtered Mochuo's son the Lesser Kagan, his brothers, and nearly all his trusted men, and raised his elder brother Mojilian, the Left Wise Prince, who became Bilge Kagan.

Gudulu's son Kultegin rallied the old tribes, slaughtered Mochuo's son the Lesser Kagan, his brothers, and nearly all his trusted men, and raised his elder brother Mojilian, the Left Wise Prince, who became Bilge Kagan.
骨咄祿 is rendered Gudulu throughout the chapter (as in the literal field), not "Kutluk".
Xiao Sha then sent his minister Ashide Yilifa to court with tribute and to attend the eastern tour.
Xiao Sha then sent his minister Ashide Jielifa to court with tribute and to attend the eastern tour.
頡利發 reads Jielifa (頡 jié), not "Yilifa". (The literal field has the same error.)
Xuanzong left the capital and at the Jiahui encampment had Yilifa and other tribal chiefs join the imperial guard and gave them bows and arrows.
Xuanzong left the capital and at the Jiahui encampment had Jielifa and other tribal chiefs join the imperial guard and gave them bows and arrows.
頡利發 reads Jielifa, not "Yilifa". (The literal field has the same error.)
Yilifa dismounted, cradled the hare, and danced, saying, "The Sage's divine prowess is beyond measure. I cannot speak of heaven, but among men there is none like him."
Jielifa dismounted, cradled the hare, and danced, saying, "The Sage's divine prowess is beyond measure. I cannot speak of heaven, but among men there is none like him."
頡利發 reads Jielifa, not "Yilifa". (The literal field has the same error.)

Should they turn vicious like watchdogs, plot together in malice, strike with assassins' stealth as Jing Ke did, or slip in as He Luo did—briefly threatening the imperial procession and staining the sacred road—even if every one of them were destroyed and their tents laid waste, how would that absolve the blame upon us?

Should they turn vicious like watchdogs, plot together in malice, strike with assassins' stealth as Jing Ke did, or slip in as Ma Heluo did—briefly threatening the imperial procession and staining the sacred road—even if every one of them were destroyed and their tents laid waste, how would that absolve the blame upon us?
何羅 is Ma (Mang) Heluo, who stole into the palace to assassinate Emperor Wu of Han; "He Luo" wrongly splits the given name Heluo as if He were a surname. (The literal field has the same error.)
In year 15, Bilge Kagan sent his minister Meluchuo to court with thirty fine horses as tribute.
In year 15, Bilge Kagan sent his minister Meiluchuo to court with thirty fine horses as tribute.
梅錄啜 romanizes as Meiluchuo (梅 méi), not "Meluchuo". (The literal field has the same error.)

The emperor praised his loyalty, feasted Meluchuo in the Hall of Purple Brightness, and rewarded him generously. He authorized a border market at Shouxiang city west of Shuofang and pledged to send hundreds of thousands of bolts of silk to the frontier each year as trade goods and gifts.

The emperor praised his loyalty, feasted Meiluchuo in the Hall of Purple Brightness, and rewarded him generously. He authorized a border market at Shouxiang city west of Shuofang and pledged to send hundreds of thousands of bolts of silk to the frontier each year as trade goods and gifts.
梅錄啜 romanizes as Meiluchuo (梅 méi), not "Meluchuo". (The literal field has the same error.)
That same year Bilge was poisoned by his minister Meluchuo. When the poison took hold, he struck first—executed Meluchuo and wiped out his entire faction before he himself died.
That same year Bilge was poisoned by his minister Meiluchuo. When the poison took hold, he struck first—executed Meiluchuo and wiped out his entire faction before he himself died.
梅錄啜 romanizes as Meiluchuo (梅 méi), not "Meluchuo". (The literal field has the same error.)
